study: Fair-value timing as the entry TRIGGER: on names the book has admitted, does buying at the moment a name turns CHEAP versus its own fair value (Z crosses below -1) beat the same name's later minute and a random other name at the same minute over the next 3 minutes, by >= +5 bp and net of cost?
registered_at: 2026-10-22, before any script, feature or outcome for this design
origin: Operator 10/22: run the fair-value timing layer as the entry trigger on every admitted-name minute, independent of the %R indicators. The filter version (fair_value_timing_prereg.json) stopped UNDERPOWERED because only 3% of pre-square entries are cheap (median entry Z +0.25): the pre-square trigger buys names that just outran their peers, so cheapness has to be its own trigger to be tested.
prior: LOW (~5-8%). Single-anchor fair-value tests failed or were underpowered (pairs 10/19, sector lead-lag 10/15, VWAP stretch 10/2); the universe of admitted names fades at every horizon (the-universe-fades-at-every-horizon), which works against buying weakness on them; at 3 minutes every bar rule tested was ~0 (THREE_MINUTE_REREAD_2026-10-21).
fair_value_model: Exactly fair_value_timing_prereg.json as amended: SIP 1-minute log returns (only when the minute and the previous one both have bars; the 09:30 bar's return excluded); peers = the 10 warehouse names most correlated with the name over the prior 10 sessions (>= 80% coverage, >= 100 shared minutes); OLS without intercept on [SPY, equal-weight peer basket (>= 5 present)] over the prior 10 sessions; Z(m) = the residual sum over the 30 completed minutes m-30 .. m-1 (>= 24 valid) / the SD of non-overlapping 30-minute residual sums over the prior 10 sessions (>= 10 blocks). The name itself needs >= 80% coverage. Code: tools/studies/fair_value_timing.py (day_task), unchanged.

populations.P1_board: LIQUID board names (amended (1)-(2), (4)): arm-row minutes 2026-09-08 .. 10-15 (28 sessions), names in the warehouse with 10 prior sessions, triggers with SIP spread <= 0.05% at T; halves A = 09-08 .. 09-25, B = 09-28 .. 10-15.
populations.P2_book_like: The 400-name seeded warehouse sample ('indicator-hist-sample') every RTH minute, 2026-05-11 .. 2026-10-15 (110 sessions), halves A <= 2026-07-29 < B - book-like names with far more power.

trigger: ONSET: Z(m) <= -1 while Z(m-1) > -1 (both computed), at a decision minute m in 10:00 .. 15:27 on an eligible minute; 15-minute refractory per name after a trigger. Entry at the SIP open of minute m, exit at the SIP close of m+2 (3 bars), as three_minute_reread.
controls: As three_minute_reread: d = the same name's later decision minute c in m+1 .. m+60 with bars at c and c+2 (seed 'fv-trigger-v1'); x = a random OTHER eligible name of the same population at the same minute with bars at m and m+2 (seed 'fv-trigger-cross'). Both required.
outcome_and_cost: net3 = SIP close of m+2 / SIP open of m - 1 - 5 bp (the live 0.05% spread cap as a round trip; 3 and 10 bp printed). Gross, 1/2/5-minute holds and MFE / MAE are information.
statistic: lift_d and lift_x per day (mean over triggers of arm - control), day-equal, day-clustered t (df = days - 1); name-day-equal lift (mean over all name-days) required > 0.
multiplicity: 2 tests (P1, P2): one-sided p 0.025 / 2 at df = days - 1.
power: Outcome-blind count step: triggers, name-days and days per half; projected MDE from the control-minute bar returns (control outcomes only). Floors per half: P1 300 triggers and 10 days; P2 1,000 triggers and 20 days; a missed floor stops that test UNDERPOWERED (no fallback).
pass: Per test, in BOTH halves: lift_d >= +5 bp and lift_x >= +5 bp, each with t >= t_crit; mean net3 > 0 at 5 bp; name-day-equal lift_d > 0; dropping the 3 names and (separately) the 3 days with the largest share keeps lift_d >= 0. FAIL: t <= -2 on d or x in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound < +5 bp on d and x in both halves (applied whenever each half has >= 2 days, regardless of floors). Otherwise UNDERPOWERED. Results are also printed against the central break-even +11 bp.
information_only: ORDER FLOW: for P1 triggers, SIP trades [T - 60 s, T) and the NBBO at T fetched (data account) and OFI60 / QI computed with the order-flow pilot's rules (keep-list, signing, cuts from the pilot's half A); lift by OFI60 tercile and for cheap-AND-flow-top-tercile. Cannot pass; a positive read needs its own prereg.
RICH onsets (Z crosses above +1) as an avoid read: lift of RICH onsets (expected negative)
Z <= -2 onsets; K = 5 / 20 peers; a 60-minute window
by hour of day; triggers within the first 30 minutes after a name's admission vs later
P1 also scored on IEX bars for the Z (live feed) with SIP outcomes
confirmation: A PASS on P2 is confirmed unchanged on the reserved held-out warehouse sample (2026-01-14 .. 04-24); a PASS on P1 is confirmed on >= 20 forward board sessions after 2026-10-22 (recorded by the desk), same code and bars. LEAD only if lift_d > 0 and lift_x > 0 with one-sided t >= 1.96 and net > 0. A LEAD then goes through the live exit replay before any paper arm.
no_retuning: the model, K = 10, the windows, the -1 onset, the refractory, the 3-bar hold, 5 bp, the populations, halves, floors and bars are fixed.
declared_deviations: completed-bar Z at the minute boundary; live acts intrabar
SIP features (P1 IEX version is information)
the board of 9/08-10/15 used the then-live admission rules and the $10 floor ($20 since 10/21)
bar-based entries carry no spread; the 5 bp cost is the live cap, not each name-minute's spread
script: tools/studies/fair_value_trigger.py (to be written): reuses fair_value_timing.day_task's model (extended to every minute of a name-day), three_minute_reread's controls and grading; count step, --score after a result-skeptic READY.
amended: 2026-10-22, before any script or data, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST (7). (1) BOARD: the ledger has no 'watch' rows in this window (stages arm / entry / trail), so an eligible P1 minute is one with an 'arm' row (any arm_ok) for the symbol in minute m. ORDER: onsets and the 15-minute refractory are computed on ALL minutes of the name-day, then only onsets at eligible minutes are kept (n is the kept onsets). (2) P1 POPULATION is declared as LIQUID board names: board names that are in the warehouse with 10 prior sessions (prior-day close >= $10 and 20-day ADV >= $20M for each of 11 sessions); the excluded board share is printed per half (it is large before 9/24 and is exactly the cheap names that carried the desk's loss). P1's x pool = names with an arm row in [m - 15, m] and SIP bars at m and m + 2 (other than the trigger name); triggers without an x are counted, and a half with > 20% of triggers lacking an x is UNDERPOWERED. (3) BOUNCE GUARD (three_minute_reread amended_2): a PASS whose lag-1 lift_d (entry at the open of m + 1, control at c + 1) is <= 0 or missing in either half is PASS_BOUNCE and does not go to confirmation. (4) SPREAD (P1 only): the NBBO at T (the last clean SIP quote <= the start of m, <= 30 s old) is fetched for every P1 trigger from the data-only account (any time of day), and only triggers with spread <= 0.05% are scored (the live cap; it was in force only from 10/3); P2 has no quotes and is scored without a spread cap (declared). (5) FIDELITY: before the count step, a test asserts that the per-minute Z equals fair_value_timing.day_task's z at every row of ai_reports/fair_value/features.json. (6) No information cell (order flow, RICH, Z <= -2, K = 5 / 20, 60-minute window, by hour, by admission time, IEX) can be promoted without its own prereg; the IEX cell uses IEX bars for the name and its peers with SIP SPY (mixed feed, declared) and prints its own n (its coverage population differs). (7) DETAILS: P1 halves by date A = 2026-09-08 .. 09-25, B = 2026-09-28 .. 10-15; 'mean net3 > 0' is the day-equal mean per half; the drop-3 share of a name (day) = its summed (arm - control) / n triggers in the half; triggers without SIP bars at m or m + 2 are counted, never silently dropped. NOTES: the P1 d control is also printed restricted to on-board control minutes, with the off-board share (seat drops follow fades; x is the cleaner P1 control); P2 reuses the three_minute_reread sample, days and halves (declared; the warehouse_confirm sample has not been read by any outcome); P1 at df 13 needs t ~2.53 and is expected UNDERPOWERED; a placebo of random pseudo-onsets matched in count per name-day is run before scoring (|t| within the per-df Bonferroni bound); the net3 condition is an absolute check beside the cost-free lift bars.
amended_2: 2026-10-22, before --score and before any trigger outcome is read (the count step reads control returns only), after result-skeptic code review FIX FIRST. (1) The P2 cross-name pool is the SAME 400-name sample as the triggers (drawn from names with today's IEX and SIP and the previous session's IEX). (2) The score path always computes the half verdict; a missed floor turns only a non-FAIL half into UNDERPOWERED (t <= -2 on d OR x stays FAIL). (3) P1 ELIGIBILITY without look-ahead: arm rows are ~12 s heartbeats, so 'an arm row in minute m' could come after the entry at the open of m; a P1 minute is eligible when an arm row has ts in [T - 60 s, T), T = the start of m; the P1 x pool is names with an arm row in [T - 16 min, T) and bars at m and m + 2. Triggers, the P1 tick fetch and the count step are rerun. (4) PLACEBO before scoring, as its own step: for every P2 trigger a pseudo-onset at a seeded random minute in the same clock hour (within 10:00-15:27) of the same name-day, scored like a trigger against its own d control; lift_d t per half must be within the two-sided Bonferroni-2 t at df = days - 1, else --score refuses. LATER, declared: (5) the drop-3-days share of a day = its summed (arm - ctrl) / n triggers in the half (as amended (7)); (6) information cells NOT run before scoring (any later run is post-hoc information): OFI terciles, RICH lift (75,543 RICH onsets collected), Z <= -2, K = 5 / 20, the 60-minute window, by hour, by admission time, IEX features, 1/2/5-minute holds, MFE / MAE; the score prints net at 3 and 10 bp and the lift against +11 bp; (7) the excluded board share is printed per half; (8) P1 tick files at the 10,000-row cap count as 'no quote'; (9) the count step checks that triggers.json and fidelity.json carry its own module shas; (10) d control minutes can fall after 15:27 (as three_minute_reread).
amended_3: 2026-10-22, operator-approved, before --score and before any trigger outcome is read, after the amended_2 placebo FAILED (P2 lift_d t -4.5 / -6.2; about -0.9 / -1.0 bp; arm -1.7 / -1.5 bp vs ctrl -0.8 / -0.4 bp, the same sign in every hour): the same-name later-minute control is biased by about -1 bp against minutes near a trigger. (1) PLACEBO-ADJUSTED d: every kept trigger (P1 and P2) gets one paired pseudo-onset exactly as amended_2 (4) (seeded minute in the same clock hour, 10:00-15:27, not m, with bars), with its own d control (seed 'fv-trigger-v1' at the pseudo minute) and its own x (same pool rule as the trigger, at the pseudo minute). lift_d is replaced by lift_d_adj per half = the day-equal mean over days of [the day's mean (arm - ctrl) over triggers - the day's mean (pseudo-arm - pseudo-ctrl) over their pseudo-onsets]; its SE and t are the day-clustered SE / t of that per-day difference (df = days - 1), which combines both SEs including their covariance (same name-days). A day needs both terms. lift_d_adj replaces lift_d in every rule: the +5 bp bar with t >= t_crit, FAIL by t <= -2, the 97.5% upper bound, and the bounce guard (lag-1 lift_d_adj from the lag-1 pseudo outcomes). The name-day-equal lift and the drop-3 names / days checks use the same paired difference restricted to the kept names / days. (2) x UNCHANGED for triggers. The PLACEBO GATE now checks x instead of d: P2 pseudo-onset lift_x (pseudo-arm - its x) t per half must be within the two-sided Bonferroni-2 t at df = days - 1, else --score refuses; the P2 pseudo lift_d is printed (it is the adjustment, not a gate). P1 pseudo lifts are printed only. (3) Unadjusted lift_d and its t are printed as information. (4) Nothing else changes; no outcome of a trigger has been read (the count step and both placebo runs read control and pseudo-onset returns only).
amended_4: 2026-10-22, before --score and before any trigger outcome is read, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST on amended_3. Declared: the size of the amended_2 placebo bias (~ -1 bp) was known when amended_3 was registered. (1) CLEAN PSEUDO-ONSET: the amended_2 pseudo minute could fall in m-3 .. m+2, sharing the move that made Z cross (or the trigger's own outcome bars), so it may measure the trigger's selection, not a control bias. The pseudo minute is now drawn (same seed tag) from the trigger's clock hour within 10:00-15:27 with |k - m| > 15 and bars at k and k + 2; if none, from the adjacent hours (previous then next) under the same rules; else none. (2) DECISION RULE fixed now: if the clean P2 pseudo lift_d (pseudo-arm - its d control) has |t| <= the two-sided Bonferroni-2 t at df = days - 1 in BOTH halves, the amended_3 premise is false and every d rule uses the RAW lift_d (as in amended_2); otherwise the amended_3 adjustment applies with the clean pseudo. P1 follows the P2 decision. (3) PAIRING per trigger: the adjusted per-day difference uses only triggers where both the trigger and its pseudo have d outcomes. (4) The P2 x gate stays (clean pseudo lift_x |t| <= the bound in both halves, else --score refuses). P1 x: a P1 PASS also needs the P1 pseudo lift_x |t| <= the bound in both halves, else the P1 verdict is UNPROVEN. (5) INFORMATION (printed by --placebo, not gating): pseudo lift_d split by k < m and k > m; an UNCONDITIONAL placebo = per P2 trigger, a seeded random other sample name at a seeded minute of the same hour with no onset of that name within 15 minutes and bars, vs its own d control. (6) The count step's projected MDE for d uses x2 (four returns) when the adjustment applies; both x sqrt2 and x2 are printed.
amended_5: 2026-10-22, before --score and before any trigger outcome is read, after result-skeptic round 2 on amended_4. (1) The paired pseudo minute must also be more than 15 minutes from EVERY onset of the same name that day (not only its own trigger): P2 onsets are all triggers; for P1 board names every onset of the name-day (eligible or not) is stored by --triggers and used. Same seed, same hour fallback. (2) The raw-vs-adjusted decision compares the pseudo lift_d t with the Bonferroni-2 bound at the d lift's own day count. (3) Declared, not changed: a pseudo before its trigger can draw a d control (k+1 .. k+60) on the trigger's minutes; the before/after split is printed.
